question: Why is the South's average daily rate lower this summer than last summer? We didn't cut prices.
system: Don't say anything that isn't clearly supported by the data. If you are unable to answer something with the data, say so. If the user is making an observation, make sure that observation is true first and correct it if not.
answer:
# Why the South's average daily rate fell

You're right that prices weren't cut. **Every category's rate went up. The overall average fell because the rental mix shifted heavily toward cheap power tools and away from expensive access and earthmoving equipment.**

## The overall drop is real

| | FY2026 (wks 14–24) | FY2027 (wks 14–24) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rental revenue | €1,920,743 | €1,940,567 | +€19,824 (+1.0%) |
| On-rent days | 56,416 | 65,080 | +8,664 (+15.4%) |
| Average daily rate | €34.05 | €29.82 | −€4.23 (−12.4%) |

## But every category's rate rose

| Category | Rate FY2026 | Rate FY2027 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| ACC Access | €53.68 | €55.92 | +4.2% |
| EAR Earthmoving | €103.36 | €107.35 | +3.9% |
| PWT Power tools | €14.55 | €15.15 | +4.1% |
| PWL Power and lighting | €29.26 | €30.49 | +4.2% |
| CON Concrete and compaction | €22.44 | €23.35 | +4.1% |

This matches the price list log. The South's new list prices took effect on 2026-04-06, which falls between the two periods compared.

## The mix shifted toward the cheapest category

| Category | Share of days FY2026 | Share of days FY2027 | Days change |
|---|---|---|---|
| PWT Power tools (cheapest, ~€15) | 41.6% | 51.5% | +10,024 (+42.7%) |
| CON Concrete and compaction | 17.9% | 18.0% | +1,590 (+15.7%) |
| PWL Power and lighting | 12.5% | 10.9% | +90 (+1.3%) |
| ACC Access | 17.3% | 12.7% | −1,491 (−15.2%) |
| EAR Earthmoving (most expensive, ~€105) | 10.7% | 6.9% | −1,549 (−25.8%) |

## Splitting the €4.23 drop

If this year's days had been charged at last year's rates, the average would have been about **€28.65**. That gives:

- **Mix effect:** −€5.40 (€34.05 → €28.65)
- **Rate effect:** +€1.17 (€28.65 → €29.82)
- **Net:** −€4.23

The category figures reconcile to the regional totals: the days match exactly, and revenue matches within rounding. All weekly files for the period are loaded, so missing data isn't distorting the comparison.

## What the data can't tell you

This data doesn't explain *why* demand moved from access and earthmoving toward power tools. That could be customer type, project mix, fleet availability, or something else. The staff notes for the period don't mention anything relevant: the only South note is about car park repainting at D06 Quenby Vale. Finding the cause would need depot-, channel-, or customer-level data.

One more point: total revenue still grew 1%, but much more slowly than on-rent days (+15.4%). That's because the extra volume came mostly from low-rate categories.
